- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.20) and forecast is below recent high, adjust upward by 1–2% to capture bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.10) and forecast is above recent high, reduce by 1–2% to avoid overreaction.  
- If forecast shows sharp upward spike followed by model overestimation, apply a 1–3 day lag correction to prevent overshoot.  
- If true outcome consistently exceeds forecast by 2–5% over 3–5 days, apply mean reversion bias: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is volatile (±0.20+), reduce forecast volatility by 10–20% to avoid overfitting to short-term noise.  
- If forecast is consistently 2–3% below true outcome over 3+ consecutive days, apply upward bias adjustment to align with recent trend.
